description: Wraps SteamSpy's single-app endpoint (request=appdetails&appid=N). Reserved for v1 per the acquisition module's open question ('rely on the tag data already in the bulk payload' was the confirmed resolution) -- this method exists in the public interface for forward compatibility but run_acquisition does not call it in v1, since tag data for the coarse-filtered candidate set is already present in the steamspy_all bulk payload captured by fetch_steamspy_catalog.
signature: def fetch_app(self, appid: int) -> tuple[int, dict]
docstring:
Fetch SteamSpy's per-app detail endpoint for one appid.

Args:
    appid: The Steam application id.

Returns:
    (status_code, payload) from HttpClient.get_json.

Note:
    Confirmed resolution of the module spec's open question 'store steamspy_appdetails per candidate, or rely on bulk tags': rely on the bulk payload. This method is retained on the client for API completeness and potential future use (e.g. refreshing a single app's SteamSpy data without a full bulk re-crawl) but is NOT invoked by run_acquisition or extract_tags in v1.
postconditions: Returns the tuple as-is from HttpClient.get_json

edge_cases.input: appid for a delisted or nonexistent app
edge_cases.expected_behavior: SteamSpy typically returns 200 with a near-empty/default-valued dict rather than 404; returned unchanged, no special-casing here

unit_tests.name: test_fetch_app_returns_stubbed_payload
unit_tests.description: A stubbed transport response is returned unchanged.
